entry.title: Combined summary - Proof-of-work based signet faucet
entry.summary: The recent introduction of `OP_CAT` in the Bitcoin signet through the [bitcoin inquisition client](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bitcoin-inquisition-25-2/838) has opened up new possibilities for blockchain scripting, particularly enabling the direct validation of Proof of Work (PoW) on-chain. This feature allows users to create complex scripts that can concatenate and validate hash bytes, a step forward in verifying PoW without external dependencies. Highlighting this advancement, a [proof-of-concept transaction](https://mempool.space/signet/tx/25deff74b7775918aa6824cfeab9121a519fb419d31ea74f6cb6a53f98cc863a) demonstrates the practical application of these capabilities. Moreover, a [Python script](https://github.com/ajtowns/bitcoin/blob/634e72cbfc0aa3f657a35c7b597f688bb2bb29a6/contrib/signet/powcoins) has been shared to facilitate users in claiming funds using PoW, ensuring that each proof is unique to the claimant through cryptographic means like signature verification and length commitments. The innovative use of transaction hashes as a form of PoW in cryptocurrency transactions offers enhanced security and prevents reusability and redundancy. Specifically, by requiring signatures that meet specific hash criteria, such as those with leading zeroes, it becomes possible to claim multiple coins in a single transaction designed to meet the PoW requirements, as exemplified by the [transaction example](https://mempool.space/tx/00000000c0747ece95852c2b7d37b09770873ed8b50fb7be2ba3d400defab06c). User interactions with the signet feature have also been detailed, showing both successful claims and errors related to difficulty settings. These anecdotes illustrate the operational specifics required to navigate the PoW claiming process effectively on the signet network. On a more accessible note, an alternative method for engaging with cryptocurrency mining has been introduced through a standalone repository, effectively lowering the barriers for newcomers to participate in mining activities. This repository is available at [https://github.com/ajtowns/powcoins](https://github.com/ajtowns/powcoins). Furthermore, the email discusses the Pay to Proof of Work (P2W) address implementation in testnet4, located at [mempool.space/testnet4/address/tb1qzsjnew5qcn75e4cqdsc6r9v8fjy5ensancqmv2l2n82p0q5f5tls758l9d](https://mempool.space/testnet4/address/tb1qzsjnew5qcn75e4cqdsc6r9v8fjy5ensancqmv2l2n82p0q5f5tls758l9d). The approach employs an operation sequence checking for signature size, providing a novel way to adjust difficulty without altering consensus rules or adding new operations. Significant updates include the ability to add a PoW challenge to any output script on the mainnet, enhancing security and adaptability. This capability is underscored by the transaction viewable at [mempool.space](https://mempool.space/tx/aba3c2ae442aa20150996ee68f9aa4da83b57a4312891078be0c2e68c50b2801), showcasing a practical application of this new feature. Additionally, the compatibility of mining software with stratumv1 ASIC miners has been established, facilitating efficient mining operations on specialized test networks. Miners can connect their equipment as described to engage in mining activities and receive rewards, with details provided for configuring systems appropriately. In summary, these developments not only enhance the functionality and security of Bitcoin's blockchain but also make participation more accessible and efficient, reflecting significant advancements in cryptocurrency technologies and their practical applications.
